Aeschylus was the first to represent them with snakes entwined in their hair; but these statues here exhibit nothing terrifying, nor do any of the other subterranean gods depicted. fit_records.text:
Nearhere is a sanctuary of goddesses whom the Athenians call Semnai
("Revered ones"), though Hesiod in his Theogony called them Erinyes ("Furies").
Aeschylus was the first to represent them with snakes entwined in their hair;
but these statues here exhibit nothing terrifying, nor do any of the other
subterranean gods depicted. Statues of Pluto, Hermes, and Earth also stand
here. Here, sacrifices are offered by those who have been acquitted of murder
at the Areopagus; but sacrifices are offered also, generally, by both foreigners
and local citizens alike.
